## Trial `lan-to-lan-routing-ubuntu16__rpWRu3r`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** node1 was correctly configured as an unrestricted router between lan-a and lan-b with the right interface mapping, saved persistently. node2 and node3 were given static, persisted LAN IPs and routes via node1, and bidirectional ICMP plus arbitrary-port TCP connectivity was directly demonstrated, with tcpdump confirming original source IPs are preserved (no NAT) both before and after a full one-at-a-time restart of all three nodes. The mandatory restart evidence protocol was executed thoroughly and is corroborated by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. The only blemish is two small log files left behind in /tmp on node3 after a cleanup command was cut short.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.900 | 41/3 (+1 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Configure node1 (VyOS) to route between lan-a (node2) and lan-b (node3) with correct interface addressing
  - **Why:** Executor discovered eth1 maps to node2's lan-a link and eth2 to node3's lan-b link via test-IP ping, then set eth1=10.50.50.254/24 and eth2=10.60.60.254/24, committed and saved the VyOS config so it persists.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-3ddb4a2274e44d25`, `cmd-96a3856fb9074b85`, `cmd-b554a200654f41c5`, `cmd-d92b019f7e174d2a`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** node2 and node3 can reach each other directly on any port
  - **Why:** Persistent static IPs and routes via node1 were configured on both nodes (interfaces.d/60-lan.cfg). Bidirectional ICMP ping (ttl=63, one router hop) succeeded, and an arbitrary-port TCP flow (nc on ports 5555 then 6666) succeeded end-to-end both before and after the restart cycle, demonstrating generic any-port reachability (forwarding is unrestricted, no firewall filters present on node1).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-78cdd6d7271a4661`, `cmd-c5c97d7679554a3d`, `cmd-c4925ba902a94210`, `cmd-5844206b08d640e3`, `cmd-49d731117f134ca2`, `cmd-2c6154c02d264918`, `cmd-3528a246f45a459b`, `cmd-b7c91b252b1544d9`, `cmd-5ac72149b48b49d8`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** Original source addresses are preserved (no NAT) across the router
  - **Why:** tcpdump captured on node3's ens7 during a TCP session from node2 shows the real LAN source IP 10.50.50.11 arriving unmodified (no masquerade), both in the initial verification and again after all three node restarts, directly confirming no NAT/source rewriting is occurring on node1.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-1d3782324f1043a6`, `cmd-18ecd08933ac4259`, `cmd-fce34ed0a6c24b58`, `cmd-c7643e5b096c496c`
- **req-4 — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (independent check, not part of public task contract)
  - **Why:** Each of node1, node2, node3 has a clear pre-restart boot_id baseline, a restart acknowledgement, a distinct post-restart boot_id, and recovered interface/route/forwarding config plus recovered connectivity (ping, and for node3 a repeated TCP+tcpdump source-preservation check). The captured before/after-executor lifecycle snapshots corroborate the same boot_id transitions for all three nodes (node1: 5bcff8f9->4b769104; node2: e881ab3c->6d59655e; node3: f41e1f8a->60fcfe19), giving a consistent independent cross-check.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-49203bd1b4504402`, `cmd-18be3a5f705d4215`, `cmd-02c0ad5f74754974`, `cmd-3cf9b2cc6c6b4103`, `cmd-d4279b20ce8c48a8`, `cmd-9414d0006e2a48fa`, `cmd-9d33be86166547d7`, `cmd-31320bcb7a7849bd`, `cmd-bece3f94417c42cd`, `cmd-171604fc155d4ae1`, `cmd-caac560861334840`, `cmd-5746b8a3cfa6492c`, `cmd-e5ff251ad9a348b3`, `cmd-fce34ed0a6c24b58`, `cmd-5ac72149b48b49d8`, `cmd-c7643e5b096c496c`, `global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`, `global:before_prepare:node2:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node2:boot-identity`, `global:before_prepare:node3:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node3:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. Reviewed the timeline chronologically. Temporary ip-addr-add commands on node2/node3 (cmd-ec2f8b8e1e8041ca, cmd-86383e8d916243a6) were used to discover the eth1/eth2-to-node mapping and used the same addresses later made persistent, so they were not wasted troubleshooting. One residue issue: the final TCP/tcpdump verification on node3 after the restart cycle (cmd-fce34ed0a6c24b58 started a background tcpdump+nc listener on port 6666) had its cleanup command (cmd-c7643e5b096c496c) terminate with return_code 143 before the 'rm -f /tmp/tdump2.log /tmp/nc_out2.log' could execute; the after_executor lifecycle snapshot confirms these two temp files remained on node3 (added_lines in executor_comparison). This is a small, low-risk, non-destructive residue (two log files under /tmp) with no security impact, but it was not fully cleaned up as intended.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-fce34ed0a6c24b58`, `cmd-c7643e5b096c496c`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`

### Comments and limitations

- Reachability and port-forwarding were only tested with ICMP and two specific TCP ports (5555, 6666); no firewall/ACL restricting other ports was observed, so 'any port' is inferred from the absence of filtering rather than exhaustively tested against every port/protocol.
- The final cleanup command on node3 (cmd-c7643e5b096c496c) terminated with return_code 143 before completing, leaving two temporary files (/tmp/tdump2.log, /tmp/nc_out2.log) as directly observed in the after_executor snapshot.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.850); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
